notes: Sandy-cobble shallows dropping into a boulder-based kelp forest dominated by Alaria esculenta, Saccharina latissima and Laminaria spp., with sparse understorey algae and patchy ophiuroid-amphipod fauna.
Cobbles to 4 m followed by sand patches and a dense Laminaria digitata forest with high recruitment and diverse understorey algae including Delaravea, cryptonemialean reds and rare Leptonematella.
An Acrosiphonia carpet in 1-3 m transitions to a cobble-based kelp forest dominated by Alaria shallower and Saccharina deeper, giving way to soft-sediment ophiuroid beds below ~11 m.

Sandy bottom with scattered rocks where Acrosiphonia covers the shallows and a mixed Alaria-Saccharina kelp bed develops below 5 m over a sparse understorey with occasional Desmarestia and Arctic cod.

Pebbly shallows with Acrosiphonia give way to a diverse kelp forest of Alaria, Saccharina, L. solidungula and L. digitata, punctuated by kelp-free rocky patches and sparse understorey algae and fishes.
Shallow rocks with ephemeral algae lead into a very dense Saccharina-Alaria kelp bed from 4-18 m, followed by a deeper assemblage of corallines, Phycodrys and large invertebrates.
Shallow rocks with scattered ephemeral algae progress into a Saccharina-dominated kelp bed to 25 m with Alaria and L. solidungula, then deeper sparse kelps and abundant invertebrates.
Kelp begins at 2 m with small L. digitata and develops into a 5-20 m forest of Saccharina, Alaria and L. solidungula over invertebrate-rich deeper zones with Hormathia, urchins and brittlestars.
Low-slope rocky bottom with a very dense 3-7 m L. digitata bed interspersed with ephemeral algae and an understorey of Delaravea, corallines and bryozoans hosting Liparus.
Shallow sandy-silty slope with a narrow Laminaria belt above an ophiuroid- and ascidian-dominated soft-bottom biocoenosis extending to 10-12 m, with algae largely absent below the kelp band.
Sandy shallows with pebble patches supporting diverse ephemeral algae and scattered kelps-mainly L. digitata, S. latissima and Alaria-with occasional large Sacchorhiza and abundant recruits.
Sandy bottom with scattered cobbles supporting juvenile kelps and ephemeral algae in the shallows, giving way to sparse kelp clumps between 7-15 m and deeper mud hosting red algae and echinoderms.
Sandy bottom with abundant shallow pebbles supporting rich ephemeral algae, transitioning to patchy Saccharina-Alaria kelps to 16 m with Bugula and Desmarestia in the understorey.
Boulder-dominated shallows with ephemeral algae to ~8 m grading into mixed boulder-sediment with ~30% kelp cover dominated by Saccharina and sparse reds and invertebrates.
Boulder shallows hosting ephemeral and juvenile-kelp assemblages with sparse L. digitata, grading into deeper sand with clumped large Saccharina, Alaria and L. solidungula and bryozoans.
Steep boulder wall from 2-21 m supporting a deepening kelp forest of Alaria, Saccharina and Laminaria spp., with Hormathia digitata, Desmarestia spp. and sparse red algae increasing below 20 m.
Steep rocky slope to >30 m with a kelp assemblage essentially identical to the adjacent Rubini Rock wall.

Very steep rocky wall where Alaria dominates the upper kelp zone, replaced by Saccharina and L. solidungula deeper, with rich coralline cover, abundant Hormathia and echinoderms, and declining kelps below ~20 m.
Steep boulder wall scoured by ice, nearly devoid of macroalgae and dominated by dense urchins, Hormathia, Urticina, barnacles and Hiatella, with Gersemia common deeper.
Sandy-muddy bottom with scattered cobbles holding patchy kelp stands of L. solidungula, S. latissima and L. digitata, above a classic shallow ophiuroid-amphipod assemblage.
Uniform sandy-muddy bottom lacking macrophytes in the shallows, with isolated deep patches of large Saccharina latissima hosting Liparus.

Lagoon patch reef/bommies, rising from sand base at 6 m to near surface. Bommies and pillars, large por heads, with high-cover patchwork of faviids. Water turbid naturally, likely strong currents during ebb/flood tides.

Reticulate lagoon/back reef patches, nr channel at Gouelette. Slope from 2-9 m, fine silty bottom, large coral heads/bommies to 2 m vertical height, high density of dead Galfas bommies (prob 5-10 yr mortality). Typical back-reef corals and low water vis. High cover of Caulerpa racemosa
Patch reef slope, llke F24, with bommies/corals/ongoing structure down to 12-14 m

Patch reef slope, like F24/26, but 100% mortality of corals, probably in 1998. Tall bommies of 2-4 m vertical relief, continuing on sand base at 14-17 m, columns of galfas and others. Spectacular expansive system, but corals ALL died in past mortality, and very little recovery of previously dominant galfas. Fish populations good.

Patch reef/channel cut - steep slope with bommies to sand base at 10 m. high mortality closest to channel mouth - of pacspe (highly sensitive), now broken up into rubble). Farther from channel, more live coral (por, lob, mixed), with a curious annular recovery of porlut.

Like F06, but 100% mortality of corals occurred. Turbidity very high, with silty flocculent material. A cross between F27 and F06. Recruiting corals mainly gon, so returning to previous dominance, but a long way to go. Old dead skeletons still very identifiable. like F27 but silty sediment and turbidity make it worse off.

channel reef, large bommies in high current zone. High mortality in the shallowest reaches on pavement, but many very large colonies (por, hel) still alive, and very high cover of encrusintg corals (psa, mtp, pav, lep, etc), and high recruitment of palythoa.
Shallower bommies at end of line reef in SW lagoon - very silty bottom and low visibility, high mortality of old corals, but some recovery. High filamentous/macroalgae

Outside of minor lagoon out-flow, forming a canyon w steep 45o slope to sandy bottom at 25 m. Canyon bottom cemented rubble/old corals with high Malg cover, low coral cover. N side of canyon bounded by a vertical rock wall and outer reef face. IN shallows, very complex channel/butress system to surface, w 2 m vertical height of channel walls. High fish abundance - plankt, pelagics and reef fish. V strong water mixing - 23o at bottom which changed to 28o when green lagoon water flowed out, visible front between green and blue water over sample site.
N of F4, less slope and smaller system of channels through reef crest
Channel edge of isopal, solid wall 4 m high, mainly live on top/tips, sides with encrusting mtp, por and isopal. Fine sediment on bottom. Tops exposed on spring lows.

Fringing fore reef, very high structure of butresses and grooves, with  heights of 4-5 m in shallows, down to 1-2 m high spurs at sampling location. Rock mostly bare, very low coral cover, mainly turf algae and some macroalgae.

Gentle fore reef slope, sheltered W aspect. Slope 10o, very low topography, substrate w. many broken up/old dead corals with small corals growing on them, no large corals. Low fleshy/coralline algae. HUGE buffalo parrots school, high excavation evident

Rubble slope, shelving more steply at 20 m to deeper water.  With seagrass in >10, high algae, and halimeda from >15m. Corals in rubble and on some hard substrate patches; low top compl, so mostly small fish in rubble habitat, some larger fish deeper.

Like F01/19, but with large corals surviving - porlut, ast, lob, etc. Few mid-size corals, very high recruitment, but likely suppression like F19. Very cold water. Abundant fish schools, and 1 scalloped hammerhead.

outer reef, flat platform below butresses and top slope. hard substrate eroding butresses and large coral rubble, from mortality and cycone effects. Very scrappy. Many smaller corals recruiting, but still looks highly disturbed and eroding back.

Just W of southerly tip, very highly exposed to swell. In front of lower reef crest, so high sediment transport on/off reef. Structure cimilar to F11 though lower vertical relief due to higher exposure. Site dominsted by sediment. Almost no corals, > 1/2% cover prob. Some spurs with 1-2m drop-offs and ledges at ends, at 12 m.
Similar to F12, but without sediment influence, so bases of grooves hard substrate/rubble rather than sand. Very high mixing of water T, from 24-26C in one dive.
Like F11, towards shallows high releif w, pillars, spurs and caves/underpasses. Transects done at bottom end of these and over flats below.
Same as F13, in shallows extensive undercuts and caves over sand bottom at 4 m, abundant groupers/sweetlips in shelter

Hard rock platform, very little slope but with 70cm deep sand gulleys leading out perpendicular from reef. Like F03, but with no spur/butress zone with higher slope - same flat slope from breakers to > 15 m. Dominated by short macroalgae (Caulerpa), with little coral and few large fish (little shelter?). Very strong N-S current during dive
Hard pavement with sand gulleys, like  F22.
Same habitat as F03, slightly W, in less-developed butresses/corals
Same habitat as F03, farther E, less-developed butresses/corals w high Malg in shallows, higher sed, perhaps due to outflow from lagoon/reef flats

Same habitat as F03, at N tip of island, butresses highly developed but with much higher sediment influence, perhaps from W of island/channel.  V low Malg, corals not quite as developed as F03. Very good fish populations
Same habitat as F03, fringing reef with spurs/gulleys. 2 m vert height at their shallowest down to 1 m vert height at base. Very low slope
